purpose: Rolling Lightsaber semantic authority using the standard Lightsaber as the recommendation baseline and preserving explicit variant advantages/tradeoffs.

vocabularyPolicy.rule: Every value in any tag-bearing field (finalTags, sharedTags, advantageTags, tradeoffTags, conditionalSynergyTags[].tag) must be an exact tag already used by at least one certified feat or certified talent. No weapon-only tags, aliases, pseudo-tags, ontology labels, or new vocabulary are permitted.
vocabularyPolicy.negativeMechanicRule: A penalty or disadvantage must not be encoded as a positive finalTag. Negative interactions belong in tradeoffTags and relativeToStandard.cons.
vocabularyPolicy.ontologyGapPolicy: Mechanics that cannot be expressed faithfully with the existing 183 feat/talent-used tags must remain plain-text unrepresentedMechanics entries. They are not tags and must never be copied into system.tags.

lightsaberComparisonPolicy.systemDesignContext: Jedi characters start with the standard lightsaber by default in this project.
lightsaberComparisonPolicy.variantSelectionRule: Do not recommend a variant merely because it is a Lightsaber. A variant should outrank the standard baseline only when one or more of its actual advantages align with character/build signals and its tradeoffs do not materially conflict with them.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard-damage lightsaber that improves successive Block checks in a round from the normal cumulative -5 to cumulative -2, but imposes -2 on Deflect checks.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals normal lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.block: Its defining advantage directly improves repeated Block checks.

pros: Repeated Block checks degrade much more slowly: cumulative -2 instead of cumulative -5.
cons: Use the Force checks made with Deflect take a -2 penalty.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for Block-heavy defensive Jedi; avoid elevating it for Deflect-focused characters.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard-damage curved-hilt lightsaber granting +1 equipment bonus on attacks of opportunity while wielded one-handed.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It deals normal lightsaber melee damage.
rationale.attack_of_opportunity: Its explicit special benefit applies to attacks of opportunity.
rationale.precision: It grants a direct +1 equipment bonus to the qualifying attack roll.

pros: +1 equipment bonus on attacks of opportunity while wielded one-handed.
cons: Its special benefit is inactive when the qualifying one-handed condition is not met.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for one-handed Jedi builds that deliberately generate or capitalize on attacks of opportunity.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Defensive lightsaber tonfa granting +2 equipment bonus on Block and Deflect checks; a phrik-laced handle also resists lightsaber DR bypass, but base damage is only 2d4.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: It remains an offensive melee lightsaber despite its defensive specialization.
rationale.block: A proficient wielder gains +2 equipment bonus on Use the Force checks made with Block.
rationale.deflect: A proficient wielder gains +2 equipment bonus on Use the Force checks made with Deflect.

pros: A phrik-laced handle prevents lightsabers from ignoring the weapon's DR.
cons: 2d4 base damage instead of the standard lightsaber's 2d8.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Strong defensive specialization when Block/Deflect reliability matters more than weapon damage.

unrepresentedMechanics.mechanic: Lightsabers do not ignore the guard shoto's damage reduction.
unrepresentedMechanics.note: No certified feat/talent-used tag precisely represents resistance to lightsaber DR bypass.

source.book: Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide

pros: May be treated as a Small weapon whenever doing so is beneficial while retaining 2d8 base damage.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Choose when a build gains a concrete benefit from Small-weapon classification and does not need two-handed wielding.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: Standard 2d8 Jedi lightsaber and comparison baseline for all Lightsaber-category recommendations.

rationale.melee: Its canonical attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: Its standard role is 2d8 melee offense.

pros: This is the standard itself: 2d8 damage with no variant-specific penalty or specialization requirement.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Default/fallback choice when no specialized lightsaber variant has a clearly supported advantage for the character.

systemDesignContext.userProjectRule: Jedi characters start with the standard lightsaber by default when they become a Jedi.
systemDesignContext.recommendationPolicy: A variant should displace the standard baseline only when its positive specialization matches the character/build strongly enough to justify its explicit tradeoffs.

assignments.canonicalMechanicSummary: 2d8 reach lightsaber pike with phrik-alloy haft; +1 square reach, -2 Block/Deflect, and conditional double-weapon functionality with Long Haft Form.

rationale.melee: Its primary attack profile is melee.
rationale.offense_melee: Its lightsaber end deals standard 2d8 melee damage.
rationale.lightsaber_polearm: It is explicitly a lightsaber pike/polearm and this tag already exists in certified feat/talent semantics.
rationale.positioning: Its +1 square reach directly changes attack/threat positioning.

pros: Phrik-alloy haft resists lightsaber DR bypass.
With Long Haft Form it can function as a double weapon with a 1d6 haft end.
cons: -2 on Use the Force checks made with Block.
-2 on Use the Force checks made with Deflect.
relativeToStandard.recommendationFit: Prefer for reach/polearm positioning builds, especially with Long Haft Form; penalize for Block/Deflect-centric defensive Jedi.

conditionalSynergyTags.reason: Double-weapon functionality is conditional rather than intrinsic and therefore is not promoted into unconditional finalTags.

unrepresentedMechanics.note: positioning captures the recommendation consequence, but no certified feat/talent-used tag precisely identifies intrinsic weapon reach.
